subject: storytime
title: The Magic Porridge Pot
about: The Brothers Grimm's 'Sweet Porridge': a poor girl is given a pot that cooks on 'Cook, little pot, cook!' and stops on 'Stop, little pot, stop!', and one day her mother forgets the stopping words and porridge fills the whole town. First graders love chanting the two magic rhymes and the idea of eating a path back home, and the lesson is said plainly: listen carefully and remember what you are told. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Chant the cooking words and the stopping words together, then ask why the pot would not stop for the mother.

book.author: the Brothers Grimm (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A magic pot, two little rhymes, and a town full of porridge.

passage.text:
Once there was a poor girl.
She lived with her mother in a town.
They had no food to eat.
One day, the girl went into the woods.
She met an old woman there.
The old woman gave her a little pot.
"This is a magic pot," she said.
"Say, Cook, little pot, cook!"
"Then it will cook sweet porridge."
"Say, Stop, little pot, stop!"
"Then it will stop."
***
The girl ran home with the pot.
"Cook, little pot, cook!" she said.
The pot began to bubble.
It filled up with sweet porridge.
The girl and her mother ate and ate.
"Stop, little pot, stop!" said the girl.
And the pot stopped.
Now they always had food to eat.
They were never hungry again.
***
One day, the girl went out to play.
Her mother was hungry.
"Cook, little pot, cook!" she said.
The pot cooked and cooked.
She ate until she was full.
"That is enough, pot!" she said.
But the pot did not stop.
Oh no!
She forgot the magic words!
***
The porridge ran over the top.
It filled the kitchen.
It ran out the door.
It ran down the street.
Soon the whole town was full of porridge!
"Help! Help!" called the mother.
Just then, the girl came home.
"Stop, little pot, stop!" she called.
And the pot stopped.
***
But the town was still full of porridge.
What could they do?
They ate it!
Everyone had to eat their way back home.
Yum, yum, yum!
The girl was glad to be home.
Listen carefully and remember what you are told.

cards.q: Who gave the girl the magic pot?
cards.note: The girl met her in the woods, and the old woman gave her the pot and taught her both rhymes.

cards.q: What did the magic pot cook?
cards.note: Say the cooking words and the pot bubbles and fills up with sweet porridge.

cards.q: What words made the pot stop?
cards.note: The cooking words start it and the stopping words end it; the mother only remembered the first rhyme.

cards.q: Where did the porridge run when the pot kept cooking?
cards.note: It ran over the top, filled the kitchen, ran out the door and down the street until the whole town was full.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The old woman in the woods gives the girl the pot before any porridge is cooked.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The town was still full of porridge, so everyone had to eat their way back home.

cards.q: How did the mother feel when the pot kept cooking?
cards.note: Oh no, and then Help, Help: the story shows her worry without saying the word.
The mother heard the magic words but did not remember them; listen carefully and remember what you are told.
Porridge is oats cooked soft in milk or water, a warm breakfast like oatmeal.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
